title: Fenix Flexin isn’t even denying using AI to make ‘Rubberz’ anymore
slides: Fenix Flexin admits AI made Rubberz — but what's real?
He says the beat started as a text prompt
His vocals were tuned by an algorithm, not engineers
Your next favorite track could be 100% synthetic
Listen once—can you still tell the difference?
thread_text:
1. He admitted it

Fenix Flexin revealed on a livestream that his track 'Rubberz' was created using AI, starting from a simple text prompt.

2. The beat's origin

The beat wasn't produced in a studio—it began as a text prompt in an AI music generator, not human-written.

3. Vocals, not human

His vocals on the track were tuned by an algorithm, not by audio engineers, raising questions about performance.

4. The next hit?

If AI can produce a track with lyrics, beat, and tuned vocals, your next favorite song might have zero human input.

5. Can you tell?

Listen to 'Rubberz' once—can you tell it's AI? If not, what does that mean for artists who rely on authenticity?

instagram.caption:
Fenix Flexin isn’t even denying it anymore—he straight-up said his track 'Rubberz' started as a text prompt. 🎤

The beat wasn't written in a studio. His vocals weren't tuned by engineers. An algorithm did both. He admitted it on a livestream, plain and simple.

If a known artist can drop a track with zero human production, the bar for “real” just moved. For anyone making music, that means your process—and your credibility—now has to compete with a prompt box. 🤖

Listen to 'Rubberz' once. Could you actually tell it was AI before he said so? 🎧
